notes:
Account overview: Sparrow Stackworks is a developer platform company (internal dev org ~450 engineers) building an in-product IDE copilot and shared CI-assisted code review assistant. They prioritize sub-200ms local edit-to-suggest latency for single-token streaming and deterministic completions via model/version pinning.

Key asks from last calls:
- Low-latency streaming from US regions with local prefix caching in front of model variants.
- Cost targets: aim to keep per-active-seat inference cost below $0.60/day (monthly benchmarking target).
- Interested in quantization profiles that preserve top-k accuracy for completions; willing to trade 2-3% quality on non-critical suggestions for 2x cost reduction.
- Need rollout controls: per-team model pinning, gradual canary for new model versions, automatic fallback to smaller quantized variants under contention.

Security/compliance: SOC2 report required; SSO/SAML already in place. KMS integration mandatory for key management; retention controls for telemetry logs (30-90 days depending on team). Data residency: US-only for production.

POC summary (Jan-Feb 2026):
- Ran 50-seat POC using hosted_api with edge routing to US-west; implemented prefix KV cache at app layer. Cache hit rate stabilized at ~42% for completion hot paths, reducing token spend by ~34%.
- Compared 8-bit and custom 4-bit quant profiles on a 2B-3B family model: 8-bit = minimal quality loss, 4-bit = noticeable regression on completions that contain type/signature info. Team prefers mixed approach: 8-bit for active sessions, 4-bit for background linting/rewrite tasks.
- Measured median latency (first token) 165ms with streaming enabled; 95th percentile spikes to 680ms under heavy CI-triggered bursts. Need routing/burst policy tweaks.
- Dev feedback: "We need deterministic completions for code actions — occasional hallucinations are dealbreakers." — Lead ML Engineer (quote).

Commercial: initial pricing asks: per-seat blended tiering, discount for committed 12-month reserved capacity (Dedicated interest). They requested an example billing model that separates editor-active vs background inference.

Documents & artifacts: pricing deck + security FAQ shared (Drive). Fireflies transcript for Jan 27 meeting (ff_2026-01-27_0a9b1c). Two internal tickets opened: INF-1129 (latency tuning), SEC-2045 (KMS integration).

Sales notes (short): choppy. AE has exec intro 2/9, procurement date target early Apr. Strong product-market fit. High probability if quantization strategy + predictable per-seat billing model hits numbers.
